knowledge-base.name: practices-api-guidelines
knowledge-base.triggers: REST API, API design, HTTP methods, status codes, versioning, pagination, error response, long-running operation, LRO, PATCH, JSON Merge Patch, API URL, resource naming, API endpoint, cursor pagination, offset pagination, API error format, 202 Accepted, idempotency
knowledge-base.overview: Concrete REST API design rules based on Microsoft Azure API Guidelines and Microsoft architecture best practices. Covers URL structure, HTTP semantics, status codes, versioning, pagination, error formats, and long-running operations.

url-structure.rule: Use nouns for resource names, not verbs. The HTTP method is the verb.
Use plural nouns for collection resources consistently.
Keep URLs lowercase. Use hyphens to separate words in path segments (not underscores, not camelCase).
Treat URL paths as case-sensitive. Return 404 for mismatched casing.
Avoid deep nesting beyond two levels. If you need /a/{id}/b/{id}/c, consider a flatter /c?bId=&aId= approach.
Query parameters handle filtering, sorting, paging, and field selection — not path segments.

method.name: GET
method.semantics: Read-only retrieval. Safe and idempotent — calling it multiple times must not change state.
method.collection: 200 OK with array body (or wrapper object with value array)
method.rule: Never use GET to modify state. Caches and proxies assume GET is safe.

method.name: POST
method.semantics: Create a resource when the service assigns the ID, or trigger an action.
method.success-code: 201 Created with Location header pointing to the new resource
method.body: Return the created resource in the response body
method.rule: POST is not inherently idempotent. Use Repeatability-Request-ID header pattern to enable safe retries.
For actions that don't fit CRUD, POST is acceptable: /orders/42/cancel

method.name: PUT
method.semantics: Create-or-replace the whole resource. The client provides the complete resource representation.
method.rule: PUT is idempotent — calling it twice with the same body must produce the same result.
Use PUT for wholesale replacement only. Use PATCH for partial updates.
If the client doesn't supply a field, it's treated as deleted/defaulted — not preserved.

method.name: PATCH
method.semantics: Partial update. Apply changes described in the request body to the existing resource.
method.format: JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396): send only the fields you want to change
method.success-code: 200 OK with the complete updated resource
method.null-semantics: Sending null for a field in PATCH means delete/clear that field.
method.rule: PATCH is not idempotent by default. Use Repeatability-Request-ID for safe retries.
Reject unknown fields and read-only fields with 400 Bad Request.
Return 409 Conflict if a create-only field doesn't match the current value (allows retry detection).

method.name: DELETE
method.rule: DELETE is idempotent. Return 204 whether the resource existed or not. Never return 404 for DELETE.
For async delete, return 202 Accepted with an operation-location header.

status-codes.code: Default success for GET, PUT, PATCH. Return with response body.
Resource created via POST or PUT. Include Location header with new resource URL.
Async operation started (LRO). Include operation-location header.
Success with no body — use for DELETE, and for actions with no meaningful response.
Client sent invalid input: missing required fields, invalid format, unknown fields.
Request is not authenticated. Client should authenticate and retry.
Authenticated but not authorized. Also use when revealing the resource's existence would be a security issue.
Resource does not exist. Do NOT use for DELETE (use 204 instead).
HTTP method not supported on this endpoint. Include Allow header listing valid methods.
State conflict: resource already exists on POST, concurrent modification, or create-only field mismatch on PATCH.
Optimistic concurrency — the ETag or If-Match condition was not met.
Request is syntactically valid but semantically wrong (business logic validation failure).
Unexpected server error. Log server-side, return minimal detail to client.
Server temporarily unavailable (overload, maintenance). Include Retry-After header.

versioning.approach: Use a required api-version query parameter in YYYY-MM-DD format.

rules.rule: api-version is required. Return 400 Bad Request with code "MissingApiVersionParameter" if omitted.
Return 400 Bad Request with code "UnsupportedApiVersionValue" for unrecognized versions.
When a preview graduates to GA, use a later date than the preview version.
Never put version numbers in URL paths (/v1/users is discouraged).
Never remove a version without a deprecation window and migration path.
Additive changes (new fields, new optional parameters) are non-breaking. Support old clients receiving new fields gracefully.

list-response-shape.rule: Return lists as JSON objects with a value array, not bare arrays. This allows adding metadata without a breaking change.

cursor-pagination.rule: Preferred for large, frequently-updated collections. nextLink is an opaque URL — clients just follow it.
Include nextLink only when more results exist. Omit it (or set to null) on the last page.
nextLink must be an absolute URL and must include the original api-version and any applied filters.
The cursor token is opaque to clients — they must not parse or construct it.
Document that resources may be skipped or duplicated across pages when underlying data changes during paging.

offset-pagination.rule: Acceptable for small, stable collections. Use skip and top query parameters.

params.param: Max items to return (minimum 1; server may cap at a maximum)

offset-pagination.rule: A server-side maximum on top is acceptable. Document it.
Offset pagination is unreliable for collections that change frequently — items can shift between pages.

error-response.rule: All errors return a consistent JSON structure under an "error" envelope key.

fields.field: Machine-readable string constant. Part of the API contract — never change it.
Human-readable explanation. May change; clients must not parse it.
The field or path that caused the error, when applicable.
Array of sub-errors, for validation failures that span multiple fields.
Recursive inner error for debugging detail. May be omitted in production.

error-response.rule: Include x-ms-error-code response header matching error.code for easy log correlation.
error.code values are part of the versioned contract. Adding new codes is non-breaking; removing or changing codes is breaking.
Never expose stack traces, internal exception messages, or database details in error responses.

long-running-operations.rule: Use LRO when 99th percentile response time exceeds 1 second, or when processing can take indeterminate time.

initiation.rule: Return 202 Accepted immediately. Do not make the client wait.
Include operation-location response header with an absolute URL to the status monitor endpoint.
Optionally include operation-id header with a unique identifier for the operation.
Accept an Operation-Id request header from the client to enable idempotent retries.

status-monitor.rule: The operation-location URL returns the current status when polled with GET.
Include retry-after header on non-terminal status responses to guide polling interval.
Retain status monitors for at least 24 hours after completion.
On Succeeded, include result in the status monitor for action-type operations.

idempotency.rule: GET, PUT, DELETE must be idempotent — the same request can be sent multiple times safely.
POST and PATCH are not idempotent by default. Use idempotency keys for operations where this matters.
Server stores the result of the first request. Subsequent identical requests return the cached result, not a duplicate.
idempotency.example: POST /payments Repeatability-Request-ID: 3ec069cb-8f45-4c88-80c0-2f98b8d87d1e Repeatability-First-Sent: Mon, 17 Mar 2024 10:00:00 GMT {"amount": 99.99, "currency": "USD"}
